title: Flight Deck Early-Warning Preflight Harness for Rollout Anomalies
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: As Redwood supports multiple release channels (stable, LTS, canary) we need a unified preflight harness that provides early detection of release regressions specific to inference serving (latency percentiles, throughput breakdowns, KV cache behavior, token cost deltas, and structured-output regressions). Flight Deck is a lightweight, orchestrated preflight runner that executes a portfolio of smoke, perf, and functional evals against candidate artifacts before they reach canary/rollout gates.

Scope: 1) Define canonical suite of preflight checks (smoke, perf microbenchmarks, delta-evals using representative prompt sets, API contract probes). 2) Implement an orchestrator service that can run suites against specific release artifacts and channels (e.g., runtime-1.20-rc1, runtime-1.20-lts-candidate). 3) Add detectors for "anomalous rollout signals" (e.g., sudden P95 latency regressions >10%, embedding quality drift on benchmark prompts, KV cache miss-rate increases, token-cost per-call drift). 4) Integrate pass/fail gates into release pipelines: block promotion when a critical detector trips; emit structured signal for downstream rollbacks and incident runbooks. 5) Surface results in Console/Slack and store historical diffs for regression fingerprinting.

Non-goals: full integration with all customer workloads, exhaustive eval coverage across every model family in the catalog (we will define representative model buckets).

Why unique: Current validation suites are fragmented (separate smoke jobs, perf harnesses, and ad-hoc evals). Flight Deck centralizes orchestration, standardizes gating thresholds per release channel, and provides early-warning detectors that are tuned for inference economics (latency x token-cost), not just functional correctness.
acceptance_criteria: A runner service exists that can accept an artifact tag and run the canonical preflight suite against a synthetic canary workload
Preflight suite includes: smoke (startup + API contract), perf microbenchmarks (p50/p95/p99), KV cache regression probes, and a delta-eval on a curated prompt set
Detectors produce a single structured verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL) and a machine-readable reason code that can be consumed by CI pipelines
Pipeline integration: a runtime-1.20 RC cannot promote to canary channel if verdict == FAIL for critical detectors
Results are pushed to Console with a short human summary and linked to raw artifacts (benchmarks, flamegraphs, sample outputs)
Historical diff storage implemented for at least 30 days to enable regression fingerprinting and triage
comments: 2025-02-21 - Arjun Patel: Spike complete. Prototyped orchestrator as a lightweight runner that spins ephemeral infra and reuses existing perf harness libs. Observed quick feedback loop (~10m per run) for a 128-token workload on a p3.2xlarge equivalent VM.
2025-02-24 - Elena Ruiz (SRE): Suggested adding KV cache miss-rate as a primary detector. We saw a past release where miss-rate jumped and cost increased 18% despite similar latency percentiles.

2025-02-26 - Tomás Becker (PM): Aligning channel thresholds. Proposal: canary FAIL if P95 regression > 15% or token-cost increase > 12%; LTS candidate stricter: P95 > 10% or quality drift detected on golden prompts.

2025-02-28 - Arjun Patel: Implemented detector scaffolding and integrated with CI. Added machine-readable reason codes (e.g., DET_LATENCY_P95, DET_KV_MISSRATE, DET_EMB_QUALITY_DRIFT). Pushing initial PR for review: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/12873
2025-03-01 - Maya Chen: Added runbook stub for Responders team: how to interpret FAIL vs WARN and immediate triage steps (collect flamegraphs, run binary search between artifacts to isolate commit).

2025-03-02 - QA: Running first full-suite run against runtime-1.20-rc1. Observed WARN for embedding delta-eval (mean cosine drop 0.018). Action: schedule focused eval and hold promotion until PM review.
